key_insight: ScenA generates multi-speaker audio scenes by conditioning a pretrained text-to-audio model on multiple reference voices, rather than relying only on explicit speaker tags or transcripts. This lets the system produce more natural conversation audio with ambient realism, closer to real-world dialogue.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between structured multi-speaker dialogue systems and real conversational audio. Existing approaches can bind speech to speakers, but they often ignore background ambience and rely on clean, speech-only pipelines.
method: Uses a text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model pretrained on large-scale in-the-wild audio.
Conditions generation directly on multiple reference voice examples to preserve speaker identity across turns.
Produces multi-speaker scenes with ambient texture instead of only isolated, clean vocal sequences.
impact: This matters because it moves dialogue generation toward realistic audio scenes that better match real-world data. For practitioners, it offers a path to richer synthetic audio for training, simulation, and media generation tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing reference voices feeding into a generative audio model

Icon set for voices, ambience, and generation flow
paper_title: Reference-Driven Multi-Speaker Audio Scene Generation from In-the-Wild Priors
paper_authors: Michael Finkelson, Daniel Segal, Eitan Richardson, Shahar Armon, Nani Goldring
